title: Game of Life
description:
Given an `m x n` grid `board` representing Conway's Game of Life, where each cell has an initial state of live (`1`) or dead (`0`), update `board` **in-place** to its next state.

Every cell interacts with its eight neighbors (horizontal, vertical, and diagonal) simultaneously according to the following four rules:

1. Any live cell with fewer than two live neighbors dies (under-population).
2. Any live cell with two or three live neighbors lives on to the next generation.
3. Any live cell with more than three live neighbors dies (over-population).
4. Any dead cell with exactly three live neighbors becomes a live cell (reproduction).

All births and deaths occur simultaneously based on the initial configuration. Aim for an `O(1)` extra space solution.
hints: Updating cells directly to 0 or 1 corrupts neighbor counts for adjacent cells that have not been processed yet.
Since each cell only stores 0 or 1 (bit 0), use bit 1 (value 2) to store the cell's next-generation state while keeping its original state in bit 0.
Read a neighbor's original state using `board[nr][nc] & 1`. After computing all next states, right-shift every cell (`board[r][c] >>= 1`) in a second pass.

examples.explanation: Each cell counts its 8 original neighbors simultaneously; cells (1,0), (1,2), (2,1), (2,2), and (3,1) are alive in the next generation.
The three live cells each have 2 live neighbors and survive; the dead cell (1,1) has 3 live neighbors and becomes alive.
